resources.string: Erase encrypted device data with a separate PIN or password
Duress protection is only available when /data has file-based encryption enabled.

Entering the duress PIN or password on the lock screen or a system device-credential prompt destroys encryption keys for all users and shuts down the device. This cannot be undone. Erasing eSIMs is also attempted, but depends on device support. A factory reset may be needed to use the device again.\n\nThe duress PIN works in PIN prompts, and the duress password works in password prompts. SIM PINs and independent app or privacy passwords do not trigger this feature. A matching normal screen lock takes priority. Do not enter a duress credential to test it on a device with data you need.
First set a screen lock PIN or password for the device owner. Switching to a pattern or removing the screen lock disables duress protection.
Requires your current screen lock. Both credentials must be entered twice. PIN auto-confirm is suspended while duress protection is enabled.
Use 4–128 digits for the PIN, or 4–128 printable English characters for the password. Use values different from your normal screen lock.
Use a credential different from your normal screen lock.
The entries do not match. Try again.
Remove both duress credentials? Your normal screen lock and device data will be kept.
Could not update duress protection. Confirm your current screen lock and try again.
